div.opener: 29 Edgeworthstown Ireland 16 Feby 1810 My dear Sir
div.p:
That a letter written by you
in last December should be answered
by one in February seems unac-
-countable unaccountable ; but in fact it has but
just reached me - It came with
a tattered pamphlet of Sir F. D Iverson
- a gentleman whom I formerly
saw in Dublin - Indeed my
Dear Sir we have such sincere
pleasure in receiving a letter from
you, that we feel impatient to
acknowledge the obligation -

You once paid us a compli-
-ment compliment upon the good fortune that
we had in being able to entertain
whilst we wrote upon subjects
of serious disquisition. We can
most sincerely say that your
relation of the Bishops episcopal
humility at a feast is in the true
style of Voltaire - In fact the
French savent conter mieux que
tout le monde -

My reviewer Sydney Smith
sees the advertisement of a
second edition of Essays on
professional education - he
had no cause for emulging
the ductus choledicus communis
of his literary gall bladder on
me except my having prefered preferred
Dugald Stewarts company to his
when I was at Edinburgh -

He may perhaps look for
some notice of his criticism in
the 2d edition - the best answer
is republication & the generous
conduct of Johnson when he
received a letter from me hoping
on my part that the sale of our
works had not been injured by
this unfair attach en gros -
30 Traités de Legislation must become
more known every day - I wish it
were in English! But I wish some
thing better. I wish that you
would write a new book from the
materials which are now heaped
together - All your care and sifting
has not done what you might
easily do by another process -

What you write in French Bentham
ought to translate!

You will see by a letter that I sent
to you by my son that we think the
same of Bexon - In a letter to
Edinburgh I expressed my sincere
wish that it might be found by the
Publick that the reviewer of Bexon
was also my reviewer - a more
dull, dry, tiresome performance
I never read - Maria did read it to
me travelling; but nothing but our
being shut up together in a chaise
could have kept us together whilst she
read I deny this - Maria E - Did I not believe that Sydney Smith
wrote the review of your book and of
Bexon I should think him a man
of wit & ability - If he wrote Peter
Plimley he must certainly be a
man of uncommon wit & humour.

- Rulhieres anarchie de Pologne
I have just ordered from your
recommendation; from the review
I should never have desired to see
is he the author of anecdotes societe de La Russie.
- I have also sent for
Simonde Sismonde
sur
Les richesse commerciales -

We are extremely desirous to
see
Talagrand Talleyrand
on public Education
- the exact title we do not know;
but you will oblige us by di-
-recting directing my son, where he can
get it -

We knew La Cretelle at Paris; -
your description of his book is
an exact description of his person
Bentham is an extraordinary
person - but I cannot concieve conceive
why you should work for him as Voltaire did
for the King of Prussia -
